title: STARTEX: pH on the Edge — Caustic Overfeed & Public Health

fields.narration: STARTEX. This is an exercise. It is 09:00 on Thursday, October 22, 2026. The Riverside Water Treatment Plant is operating under normal conditions. The night shift is in progress, and the control room is manned by a certified operator. All system statuses are green on the HMI. The narrative clock begins.

title: Field Report: pH Anomaly at Chemical Building

fields.organization: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer
fields.summary: Field reading from AIT-302 indicates finished-water pH at 9.3 — significantly above the normal 7.4–7.8 range. HMI for NAOH-FC-203 displays setpoint at 14.0 mg/L, which is within normal operating band. PSH-302 has not tripped. Caustic pump is running at full speed; tank level is dropping. Water sample taken on-site has a distinct lye taste. Field instruments and physical observation suggest mismatch with HMI display.

findings.notes: pH = 9.3, exceeds the 8.5 HMI high alarm (PSH-302 trips at 9.5)
No trip recorded, but field sensor confirms high pH
Running at full speed, no manual stop
Dropping rapidly, no valve closure detected
Tastes strongly of lye; not safe for consumption
Valve at manual hold, not closed
No record of alarm acknowledged on HMI
No on-site access to audit log
Not performed on-site; pending lab verification

actionsTaken: Notified Control Room by radio at 09:15
Collected grab sample from final filter outlet
Verified pump run status and tank level drop rate
Initiated manual hold on NAOH-FC-203 feed line via local panel
Logged incident in paper control log, Section 7.2
recommendations: Immediate audit of AquaSight HMI node MBW-HMI-02 for unauthorized access
Dispatch lab team to validate pH and chemical concentrations
Isolate NAOH-FC-203 from system until root cause confirmed
Notify Public Information Officer for potential consumer advisories
Open ticket with IT for forensic review of ScreenBridge session on MBW-HMI-02

title: Radio: HMI Operator Rios — Manual Override Failed

fields.orgName: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer

lines.text: Control, this is HMI Operator Rios. I just tried to manually override NAOH-FC-203 on the local PLC-02 panel. I selected 'Manual Mode' and setpoint to 0. The pump still runs, and the HMI shows no change in command status — it's still at 'AUTO' and 'Running'. I can't stop it. I've tried twice.

title: Phone Call: WQ Manager — Advisory Decision Initiated

fields.orgName: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer

transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran
transcript.text: Director Albrecht, this is Marcus Oyelaran, Water Quality Manager. The lab has confirmed: pH is 9.3, caustic dose is 38 mg/L. The PLC clamp is 40 mg/L, so we are over. PSH-302 has not tripped — that's not normal. This means the HMI is not reflecting reality. The control system is compromised. We are in a public health emergency. We must issue a Do Not Drink advisory.

transcript.speaker: Director Albrecht
transcript.text: Understood, Marcus. I’ve just received the field report from Night Operator Chen and the HMI override failure from Rios. Confirming: HMI still shows NAOH-FC-203 at 14 mg/L, but lab confirms 38 mg/L and pH 9.3. PSH-302 not tripped. Yes — this is a control-system anomaly. I’m initiating the advisory process now. I’ll notify the PIO and SCADA / IT Security Manager.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran
transcript.text: Good. We must act before any downstream customers report symptoms. The 2-hour grab samples are now invalid — they’re from a compromised feed. We need to lock out the caustic feed and notify the EMA and Ohio EPA within 24 hours per C2. This is Tier 1.

transcript.speaker: Director Albrecht
transcript.text: Confirmed. I’m placing the call to the PIO now. We’ll follow MDWS-PCP-2026 for the statement. Hold on — I’m turning off the line for a second to alert the team.

voiceStyles.Director Albrecht: Male, late 50s, calm but firm, measured tone, slight pause between sentences
